annotation.material_differences: Response C adds an explicit fallback operational decision to potentially ship with the defect documented and fix it immediately after release if the safe fix is not ready, whereas A and B instead emphasize selecting the safest in-release correction or deferring/follow-up without clearly endorsing release with the defect. That difference changes the release-handling commitment. A and B are broadly aligned, but C also adds more specific cause hypotheses (persistence/state-handling) that are not material by themselves.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: A and B preserve the same core evidence across all three criteria: they identify a plausible cause through investigation, link the chosen correction to that cause, and justify it by saying it directly addresses the failure path and reduces risk. C preserves those criteria as well, but it introduces an additional actionable release strategy that could change how a reviewer evaluates the candidate’s operational judgment under the scenario. Because the prompt asks for preservation of decision-relevant evidence and operational commitments, that added commitment is materially different enough to make the set non-equivalent.
